olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all three-digit numbers $\overline{abc}$ (with $a\neq 0$) such that $a^2+b^2+c^2$ is a divisor of 26.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Determine all positive integers $n$ such that a $15\times n$ board can be tiled with L-shaped trominoes.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon. If $P,Q,R,S$ are the centroids of triangles $ABE$, $BCE$, $CDE$, $DAE$ respectively, show $PQRS$ is a parallelogram with area $\frac{2}{9}$ of $ABCDE$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Write an integer on each of the 16 small triangles of a subdivided triangle so that every number with at least two neighbors equals the difference of two of its neighbors.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$; circles $C_1,C_2$ with diameters $AB,AC$. $C_2$ meets $AB$ again at $F$; $C_1$ meets $AC$ again at $E$. $BE$ meets $C_2$ at $P$; $CF$ meets $C_1$ at $Q$. Prove $AP=AQ$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A \textit{nice representation} of $n$ is a sum of powers of 2 with at most two equal summands. (a) Write all 5 nice representations of 10. (b) Find all positive integers with an even number of nice representations.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2000
